answer: At dawn each agent must dock at a shared harbor of reputation: before any transaction, it stakes a small bond tied to a verified history of useful work, and the bond is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates. A Sybil attacker must fund a separate stake and a separate believable history for every fake, so the cost of flooding the market rises with each copy while the gain stays flat; by the time the network reaches its zenith of activity, minting sock puppets costs more than any fraud could return.
